I am 61 years old, and I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I never went to school, so I do not read books or calculate kilograms, but I know my land and I know cotton. My household has four people, and cotton is what puts food on the table. I grow cotton on all 9 mu because that is what my family has always done, and I do not take risks with new crops.

This year, I will do what I did last year. In early April, when the soil warms up, I will rotary till the fields. I will buy improved cotton seeds from the shop — the kind my neighbor down the road uses, guoxinmian or something similar. I plant about two jin per mu. For fertilizer, I will spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. That is about 100 jin, same as always. The bag says it has some of everything. If the cotton looks yellow at flowering time, I might throw on a little urea, but fertilizer costs money, and I need to keep cash in my pocket for my family.

I have a well, so I can irrigate, but pumping costs electricity. I will water twice — once after planting if the spring is dry, and once when the cotton is flowering. If the summer is very hot, maybe three times, but twice has been enough most years. The bollworms and aphids are the biggest problem. I will spray pesticide about twelve times from June to August. It hurts to spend so much on chemicals, but without it, the insects will destroy everything. I do all the spraying myself or with my son.

I expect to pick about 500 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather is normal. I harvest by hand starting in late September and going into October. My wife and I pick, and my family helps. Last year was fine, so I see no reason to change anything. I would rather waste a little money on fertilizer than risk a bad year.
